text:
123
Gestern Abend spät erhielt ich per Estaffette beigehende Schrei¬
ben des p Kunckel, welches ich Ewr Hochfürstliche Durchlaucht dabei
lezt einreiche, und um Hochdero Verhaltungs befehle bitte
Nothwendig ist es allerdings mit dem v. Otocki ein Abkommen zu treffen
und wann dies durch gütlichen Vergleich bewürckt werden könte, daß
Otocki mit 1500 oder 2000 rt. zufrieden wäre, so wären es eine
Vorteilhafte wünschens werthe Sache. Euer Hochfürstliche Durchlaucht
höchste Ermeßen stelle ich es anheim — ob dem Kunckel die Vollmacht
zum Vergleich gegeben werden soll.
daß übrigens der Kunckel und Jentsch sich so entgegen zu handeln
ſcheinen erregt meine große Beſorgnis — ich fürchte daß Kunckel
durch seine Wehementes Gebaren dumm Zeug und Jentsch aus
Bosheit, Intriguen machen wird, die nachteilig werden können.
Mein unvergreiflicher Rath ist die Menschen wohl zu instruiren
und in ihren Schrancken zu weisen.
Glenck ist gestern nicht mehr zu mich gekommen und hatt so
gar die Kontopper Rechnungen hier gelaßen, die über alles
in dieser Sache einen Aufschlus gaben.
Breslau den 23ten April 1804
v Triebenfeld

translation.en:
123 Late yesterday evening I received by express courier the enclosed letter from Kunkel, which I herewith [uncertain: lezt] submit to Your Most Serene Highness, requesting Your instructions as to how I am to conduct myself. It is indeed necessary to come to an arrangement with von Otocki, and if this could be brought about by an amicable settlement, such that Otocki were content with 1500 or 2,000 Rthl., it would be an advantageous and desirable thing. I leave it to Your Most Serene Highness's supreme judgement — whether the power of attorney for the settlement is to be given to Kunkel.

That Kunkel and Jentsch, moreover, appear to be acting so much against one another arouses my great apprehension — I fear that Kunkel, by his vehement conduct, will do foolish things, and that Jentsch, out of malice, will make intrigues, which may prove prejudicial. My humble counsel is to instruct these men well and to keep them within their bounds.

Glenck did not come to me again yesterday, and has even left the Konotop accounts behind here, which gave full information upon everything in this matter.

Wrocław, the 23rd of April 1804

v Triebenfeld

text_english:
123 Late yesterday evening I received by express courier the enclosed letter from Kunkel, which I herewith [uncertain: lezt] submit to Your Most Serene Highness, requesting Your instructions as to how I am to conduct myself. It is indeed necessary to come to an arrangement with von Otocki, and if this could be brought about by an amicable settlement, such that Otocki were content with 1500 or 2,000 Rthl., it would be an advantageous and desirable thing. I leave it to Your Most Serene Highness's supreme judgement — whether the power of attorney for the settlement is to be given to Kunkel.

That Kunkel and Jentsch, moreover, appear to be acting so much against one another arouses my great apprehension — I fear that Kunkel, by his vehement conduct, will do foolish things, and that Jentsch, out of malice, will make intrigues, which may prove prejudicial. My humble counsel is to instruct these men well and to keep them within their bounds.

Glenck did not come to me again yesterday, and has even left the Konotop accounts behind here, which gave full information upon everything in this matter.

Wrocław, the 23rd of April 1804

v Triebenfeld
summary_en: Triebenfeld submits a letter from Kunkel that arrived by express courier and asks for instructions on how to proceed. He considers an arrangement with Otocki necessary; an amicable settlement, in which Otocki would be satisfied with 1500 or 2,000 Rthl, would be advantageous, he says. Whether Kunkel should be given a power of attorney to settle he leaves to the Prince. He fears that Kunkel and Jentsch are working against each other and advises instructing both. Glenck did not come again, but left behind the accounts from Konotop, which explain everything.
summary_de: Triebenfeld reicht ein per Estaffette eingegangenes Schreiben Kunckels ein und bittet um Verhaltungsbefehle. Er hält ein Abkommen mit Otocki für nötig; ein gütlicher Vergleich, bei dem Otocki mit 1500 oder 2000 Rthl zufrieden wäre, sei vorteilhaft. Ob Kunkel Vollmacht zum Vergleich erhalten soll, stellt er dem Fürsten anheim. Er fürchtet, dass Kunkel und Jentsch gegeneinander handeln, und rät, beide zu instruieren. Glenck kam nicht mehr, ließ aber die Rechnungen von Konotop zurück, die über alles Aufschluss geben.

reading.notes: Triebenfeld sends on to the Prince a letter from Kunckel that came by Estaffette and asks for instructions. He advises settling with Otocki and says a friendly settlement at 1500 or 2000 rt would be good. He leaves it to the Prince whether Kunckel should get the power of attorney for the settlement. He fears that Kunckel and Jentsch are working against each other and advises instructing both of them. Glenck did not come back and left the Konotop accounts behind, which explain the whole matter. Nothing in the letter concerns Trąbczyn.
